newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-STRANG POSES PROBLEMS FOR ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-STRANG POSES PROBLEMS FOR ENGLAND.

text.p: Leg spinner Paul Strang bowled Zimbabwe back into the game on the third day of the first test against England at Queen's Club on Friday.

Strang took the wickets of Alec Stewart (48) and Graham Thorpe (13) to add to his dismissal of Mike Atherton on Thursday evening. At tea England were 231 for four in reply to Zimbabwe's first innings total of 376.

Strang ended a partnership of 68 between Stewart and Hussain when he won an lbw appeal against Stewart. The Surrey batsman had looked in fine form, striking eight boundaries from 123 balls, and was a little unlucky to be given out sweeping on the front foot.
But Strang fully deserved the wicket of Thorpe who was bamboozled by a googly and caught at slip by Zimbabwe captain Alistair Campbell with the score on 180.
Hussain took the attack to the bowlers and, having been dropped at short-leg off Strang from the first ball he faced, reached his half century from 131 balls with six fours.
At tea Hussain had scored 61 with John Crawley on 19.
